page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Two small "NB." and "Censura." notes stand in the right margin beside the text. Top right: page number 87. Top centre: running head. Bottom: catchword "post" at the right and signature "F 4" at the left of the foot.

main_text.p: uiorem[?] commendari reperio, idq; duabus aut tribus horis post. Postero igitur die hesternā crapula disturbati diligenter animadvertent, num excrementa in illis & humores crudi sint revocati & propulsi ad centrum, an vero ventriculum eiusque orificium afficiant? illic exercitium & motus ante cibum, vel somnus ad tertiam etiam diei partem, teste Hipp. absque interruptione extractus laudatur: hic vomit*, inedia, fomenta, linimenta vel frictiones circa ventriculi regionem magis commendantur. Unde male sanitati consulunt, qui ventriculo ex immodica fortioris meri potione aestuantiCensura. & sitientiNB. refrigerium quaerunt potu frigido aquae vel cerevisiae, quam ad aliquot saepe mensuras a Germanis ingurgitari ieiuno stomacho passim videas.

Sed dum calorem eo remedio deferbere putant, feruentiorem eum paulò post & auctioremNB. deprehendunt, quo enim plus bibunt, eo plus sitire incipiunt, non secus ac in lapidibus excalfactis videmus, qui, si aqua frigidissima asperguntur, multò sentiuntur calidiores, nutriente videlicet in ipsis humida substantia aridam caliditatem, ut ita hoc medicandi ventriculo excalfacto modo nihil fit nocenti*.
Qui de noctu sitiunt, decenti & conuenienti utantur potu, & postea redormiant, id enim bonum esse ipse Hipp. asseruit. Qui tamen adhuc graviori siti tentantur atque premuntur

page.notes: The first word of the page, "uiorem", is a fragment from the previous line and is doubtful; its initial letter and the reading are uncertain. Asterisks after "vomit" and "nocenti" are printed reference marks, but their footnote text is not printed on this page. Marginal notes: "Censura." (beside "aestuanti") and two "NB." (beside "sitienti" and "auctiorem"); the "Censura." and first "NB." are set in a heavy italic/black face. Printed "fitiunt", "fitire" were read as sitiunt, sitire (long s). Catchword "post" and signature "F 4" are at the foot.
